headline: The latest audited security report remains Reuters' Oct 23 article: the Washington Institute map recorded 28 confirmed and reported attacks in Hormuz-area waters during October and 113 since Feb 28; UKMTO warns voluntary ship reporting misses incidents. No newer directly comparable LNG-only weekly transit count was identified; Kpler's three Jul 27-Aug 2 transits remain historical context. The Oct 21 tanker-fire claim and Kpler's 18 attacks over two weeks remain attributed.

evidence.title: Three oil tankers hit by projectiles in Hormuz strait on Tuesday, Marisks says
evidence.note: Re-scraped Oct 17; historical report retained with its original publication date. Marisks reported three Liberian-flagged oil tankers were struck by unknown projectiles while transiting Hormuz on Sep 29. Reuters names Al Ruwais, Mersin Prosperity and Sinbad; Marisks said AIS transponders were off.

evidence.title: Iran says it receives US response to latest proposal
evidence.note: Re-scraped Oct 17; historical report retained with its original publication date. Iran said it received a US response to its latest proposal. An official briefed on the talks said the parties disagree about the sequence of steps; no reopening agreement was reported.

evidence.title: Qatar-linked LNG traffic through Hormuz strait picks up despite conflict
evidence.note: Re-scraped Oct 17; historical report retained with its original publication date. Reuters/LSEG/Kpler tracked GasLog Skagen off Sri Lanka Sep 27 with a Ras Laffan cargo. Al Shamal reappeared outside Hormuz around Sep 24-25; Al Ghashamiya delivered to Dahej Sep 24. The report describes individual sightings and dark AIS transits, not a complete comparable weekly LNG count.

evidence.title: Oil jumps 4% on reports China halts fuel exports, US troops head to Middle East | live
evidence.note: Re-reviewed Oct 12 at a Reuters syndication on Euronext: China suspended fuel-product exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau; Oct 1 settlement values are historical.

Hormuz ship attacks surge: Are increased oil exports sustainable? | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
Oil prices settle down as IEA agrees to accelerate oil stock release | Reuters
evidence.note: Reuters reports oil settled lower on Oct 7 after the IEA agreed to accelerate oil-stock releases and a surprise US crude draw; Houthi strikes heightened supply concerns.

evidence.title: Qatar extends force majeure notices on LNG supply to Edison, Asian clients including Bangladesh | The Business Standard
evidence.note: Reuters reports Edison expects no QatarEnergy LNG cargoes until early December and some Asian clients were notified through November; buyer notices are not a measured total output loss.

evidence.title: September LNG shipments through Hormuz hit highest since start of US-Iran war
evidence.note: Kpler counted 21 LNG cargoes exiting Hormuz in September, up from 15 in June. Dark AIS transits may not be captured, so this is a tracked count rather than complete traffic.

evidence.title: More Qatari LNG cargoes transit Strait of Hormuz despite ongoing risks | Reuters
evidence.note: Kpler/LSEG tracked four Qatar-loaded LNG vessels reappearing outside the strait on Oct 2-3. This is a dated sighting set, not four additional monthly transits; dark AIS means counts are incomplete.

evidence.title: Gulf oil flows rise to average 81% of pre-war rate in September, data shows | Reuters
evidence.note: Reuters distinguishes Vortexa crude, condensate and refined fuels including LPG (19.2 million bpd) from Kpler total September oil exports (18.6 million bpd) and Kpler combined crude plus condensate exports for seven Gulf states (14.7 million bpd). These are regional exports, not a Hormuz transit count.

evidence.title: Attacks on tankers in Hormuz hit highest of any week since start of Iran war, sources say | Reuters
evidence.note: Reuters reports at least 12 tanker attacks in Sep 28-Oct 5, the highest weekly number since the war began; IMO tallied nine incidents.

evidence.title: Iran says US response to its proposal to reopen Hormuz was 'insufficient' | Reuters
evidence.note: Reuters reports Iran’s security chief said the US response to seven reopening conditions was insufficient; no reopening agreement was reported.

evidence.title: Houthi strike on Saudi airport kills 12, worst attack on kingdom in a decade | Reuters
evidence.note: Reuters reports at least 12 killed and more than 300 wounded at Riyadh airport on Oct 10; the article said the Houthis had not claimed responsibility for that attack at publication.

evidence.title: Iran shifting tactics to step up attacks on shipping before US vote, officials say
evidence.note: Reviewed Oct 15: Iranian officials said new tactics began about 10 days earlier; Reuters reported at least five incidents in the prior 48 hours involving tankers and commercial ships, including waters off Qatar and the UAE. This is incident reporting, not a transit count. Oct 22 exact-page retrieval failed at the Firecrawl API DNS lookup and the browser reader could not open the canonical Reuters URL; carry the prior approved review without extending its checked date.

evidence.title: Container ship sinks near Hormuz after being hit by projectile, sources say
evidence.note: Reviewed Oct 15: Reuters reported the Singapore-flagged GFS Pride was damaged by a projectile, caught fire and sank while transiting; all 21 crew were evacuated without injuries. Cape Dao, hit Sep 23, separately sank later, with one crew member dead. Oct 22 exact-page retrieval failed at the Firecrawl API DNS lookup and the browser reader could not open the canonical Reuters URL; carry the prior approved review without extending its checked date.

evidence.title: Oil prices climb as traders weigh Saudi supply risk, Russian diesel flow
evidence.note: Reviewed Oct 15: Reuters reported Brent settled at $106.06/bbl (+0.35%) and WTI at $95.09/bbl (+1.01%) on Oct 14 as traders weighed Saudi supply and shipping risks. Oct 22 exact-page retrieval failed at the Firecrawl API DNS lookup and the browser reader could not open the canonical Reuters URL; carry the prior approved review without extending its checked date.

evidence.title: Oil touches $110 a barrel for first time since May on Middle East, Russia supply fears
evidence.note: Exact Reuters page review confirms Oct 16 Brent settlement at $109.86/bbl and WTI at $101.41/bbl; the article discusses Middle East and Russian supply concerns, not a new Hormuz incident.

evidence.title: Supertanker rates fall from record highs
evidence.note: Exact Reuters page review confirms the Oct 16 Gulf of Oman-to-China VLCC rate near Worldscale 776, down from 841 the prior week. This is not a USD/bbl cost.

evidence.title: BRIDS Daily Economic & Fixed Income Update Friday, October 16, 2026
evidence.note: Exact BRI Danareksa report review confirms Indonesia 10-year government yield at 7.245% on Oct 15, versus 7.209% the prior day.

evidence.title: Thailand 10-Year Government Bond Yield - Quote - Chart - Historical Data - News
evidence.note: Trading Economics reports Thailand 10-year government yield at 2.24% on Oct 23, unchanged from the prior session.

evidence.title: Philippines 10-Year Government Bond Yield - Quote - Chart - Historical Data - News
evidence.note: Exact Trading Economics page review on Oct 25: the dated Oct 23 row reports 8.12%, up 0.06 percentage points from the previous session. The page also displayed an undated live Actual value; the audited observation is the dated Oct 23 row.

evidence.title: Oil rises on Middle East supply worries | Reuters
evidence.note: Reuters reports that Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said a supertanker caught fire after striking a mine south of Hormuz, according to Iranian media; Kpler separately reported at least 18 vessel attacks over two weeks. These remain source-attributed claims.

evidence.title: Ship attacks in Strait of Hormuz hit record high in October
evidence.note: Reuters reported Oct 23 that the Washington Institute map recorded 28 confirmed and reported attacks in Hormuz-area waters during October and 113 since Feb 28. UKMTO reported voluntary ship reporting gaps. This is an incident tally, not a transit count.
